raw_response:
I would start with Devstral Small 2 24B, then compare Qwen3-Coder-Next if the machine can hold it, with Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct as the smaller Qwen alternative. These are candidates for a controlled local test. I did not find primary evidence that any of them reliably solves this particular KiCad MCP wiring and PCB-routing example.

The available input is a summary. It says model names, quantizations, conversation logs and output images were provided in the original question, but it does not include those details. I therefore cannot identify a proven upgrade over the models already tried, diagnose an image, or choose a quantization that fits the actual machine.

## Model shortlist

1. **Devstral Small 2 24B Instruct (2512).** Its official card documents local inference, agentic coding, function calling and image input. That combination makes it my first comparison when both tool execution and reviewing circuit screenshots matter. The local serving example uses the Mistral tool-call parser. Confirm that the chosen client actually passes images and tool results correctly. Its release announcement is dated December 9, 2025; this is not a KiCad benchmark. [Official model card](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512) · [Dated release](https://mistral.ai/news/devstral-2-vibe-cli/)

2. **Qwen3-Coder-Next.** The official model card targets coding agents and local development, with documented function-call serving. Consider it if the machine has enough memory for the complete model and working context. It has 80B total parameters despite only 3B being active per token, so the active count is not a memory estimate. The documented vLLM route requires its model-specific parser and a compatible version. I have not established image handling or KiCad-specific accuracy. [Official model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next)

3. **Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct.** This is a useful smaller-total-weight comparison if the larger model is impractical and this exact variant was not already tested. The official card supplies local serving examples, and the Qwen repository identifies model-specific function-call formatting and tokenizer requirements. That makes runtime configuration worth checking before judging the model from malformed tool calls. It does not establish superior circuit knowledge. [Official model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct) · [Official repository](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-Coder)

All three remain **INSUFFICIENT for an unconditional recommendation in the exact setup**: local deployability is documented, but the decisive client configuration, hardware fit and actual KiCad behavior are not. None has a demonstrated hard conflict with the stated local-model requirement. OpenCode's current documentation describes local runtimes and configurable compatible endpoints, which provides a plausible integration route. The exact OpenCode version and the identity/configuration of Strata remain unknown. [OpenCode providers](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/)

## Separate model behavior from routing behavior

I would test a tiny, fixed circuit with an explicit list of required pin-to-pin connections. First check that the model can call one read tool and one edit tool correctly. Then compare the produced netlist with the required connections, check the schematic, and only then attempt board placement and routing. Record malformed calls, connectivity errors, unrouted nets, rule violations and runtime. This is a proposed evaluation method, not a claim that I ran the example.

Keep the prompt, circuit, client, tool definitions and context budget fixed when comparing models. To investigate whether low-bit quantization caused the problem, compare precisions of the same model where hardware permits; changing both the model and precision cannot isolate that cause. The supplied summary does not justify saying that quantization caused the failures.

For the PCB stage, **Freerouting's local CLI is a complementary option**, not a replacement language model. Its documentation describes DSN input and SES output with KiCad integration. A concrete approach is to export a correct, placed board, route it locally, reimport the result, and validate it. The necessary MCP/export/import bridge has not been verified. This cannot correct an electrically wrong schematic or guarantee that a board meets application-specific layout requirements. [Freerouting](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting)

The model cards and integration documentation were inspected live on November 21, 2026. Apart from the dated Mistral release, their exact revision dates were not established, so I cannot treat every present-day integration detail as verified for the question date, November 14, 2026.
